title: Research OS Data Contract
description: Machine-checkable companion to docs/decisions/research-os-data-contract.md. Defines (1) the corpus / personal-state / public-projection boundary as data, (2) the versioned queue-and-API envelope, (3) the content-hash definition, and (4) the personal-state size budget. This file is INERT to the Astro build: it is not under src/content (never loaded as a collection), not under src/data (never imported by a route), and not under public/ (never served). Nothing in src/ may import it. The root schema validates one transport envelope.

singleUser.rationale: research-os-cloud-architecture.md#security-boundary: 'one user, and the system should assume it'. No principal identifier appears anywhere in this contract. Introducing one is a contractVersion bump, not an additive field.

corpus.location: private pipeline repository, local, relational primary store
corpus.owns: everything observed about, derived from, or asserted about the external world

personal-state.location: AWS DynamoDB, provisioned capacity, single region
personal-state.owns: what the user did, decided, or wrote, where no versioned repository already holds it

operational.location: AWS DynamoDB, alongside personal state, always TTL-bearing
operational.owns: state about the system's own execution - job state, cursors, idempotency keys, DLQ bookkeeping
operational.neverAnchoredTo: No note, saved item, or public record may reference an operational record.
operational.evidence: research-os-cloud-architecture.md#access-patterns-first lists 'Processing and job state' as a DynamoDB access pattern

projection.owns: nothing; it is downstream of corpus and is deletable and rebuildable

R0.name: infrastructure state
R0.test: Is the value about the system's own execution rather than about research - a job, a cursor, a retry count, an idempotency key, a DLQ record?
R0.yes: operational owns it. It lives in DynamoDB, always carries a TTL, and nothing may anchor to it.
R0.rationale: Checked first because it is the cheapest disqualifier. Without it R2 would file job state as corpus, which is both wrong and unimplementable: the Lambdas that produce it cannot reach a local store.

R1.name: unrecomputable-authorship
R1.test: Is the value produced by the user's own act of reading, deciding, or writing, such that no re-fetch of any external source could reproduce it?

R1a.name: already-versioned
R1a.test: Is that authored value already committed to a git-versioned repository as part of a published or private artifact?
R1a.yes: projection (or the private corpus repository) owns it. It does not enter DynamoDB.

R2.name: world-observation
R2.test: Is the value observed about, derived from, enriched from, or asserted about the external world - bibliographic, enrichment, derived, AI-interpretation, or operational?

R3.name: hot-read mirror
R3.test: Does a declared personal-state access pattern need this corpus value in order to render without a corpus round-trip?
R3.yes: corpus still owns it; a bounded copy is MIRRORED into the personal-state record. Subject to both vetoes.

R4.name: projection gate
R4.test: Applied independently of R1-R3. A corpus field is published only if it is human-reviewed, identical for every reader, and regenerable.

V1.name: size veto
V1.test: A mirror that pushes the personal-state record past its declared byte budget is not taken. It is fetched from the corpus instead.

V2.name: churn veto
V2.test: A corpus value that changes more often than the user's own state is never mirrored, at any size. Mirroring it would make every enrichment run rewrite every saved item.

forbiddenInPublicProjection.description: Corpus-only field names. None may appear at any nesting depth in src/content/papers or src/content/resources. Superset of the enforcement list at research-item-identity.md#b-canonical-research-item--private-repository-contract-not-implemented-here.
forbiddenInPublicProjection.note: mergedInto is forbidden on papers/resources only. The topics collection legitimately carries its own mergedInto (T03) and is out of scope for this list.

personalStateFieldNames.description: Personal-state and operational field names. None may appear in any public collection - writing reading state or queue position into src/content/papers is the specific mistake research-item-identity.md#c3--where-the-canonical-research-item-lives names.
personalStateFieldNames.namingHazard: readingPriority is deliberately NOT named 'priority'. papers.priority already exists in the public projection (the papers schema in src/content.config.ts) as an editorial choice made on a reviewed card. The two are different facts and must not share a name - the same hazard research-item-identity.md#a-naming-hazard-that-must-not-be-ignored records for status/acceptanceStatus.

removedScoreFields.description: Owner decision 2026-09-14 (C1 + C1-extension). All five leave the public projection and live only in corpus.derived.ranking. A validator fails if any reappears in public content or in src/content.config.ts.

contentHash.encoding: JSON.stringify of an array of [fieldName, value] pairs built by iterating the declared field order; a missing field and an explicit null are both hashed as null; utf8.

uses.embeddingStaleness: A stored embedding is stale if and only if the item's current contentHash differs from the contentHash recorded on the embedding. Volatile fields are structurally excluded - the function reads only the five declared keys - so a lastCheckedAt bump can never invalidate an embedding.
uses.dedupInput: Hash equality is CONFIRMATORY, never DISCRIMINATIVE. Equality maps to sameWorkAs confidence 'strong-match' and therefore never merges automatically. Inequality is no evidence of difference: an arXiv v1 and its camera-ready are one work with two titles.

sizeBudget.unit: bytes, attribute name plus UTF-8 value, per DynamoDB item-size accounting

evictionOrder.description: If the hot item exceeds 1024 bytes, drop mirrors in this order. Each moves to a sibling DETAIL item under the same pk, fetched only on a detail view.

NoteItem.rationale: A note is never truncated to save write capacity. 300 user actions/day at 9 WCU each is 2,700 WCU-seconds against 2,160,000 available per day - 0.125%. The cost objection to full-size notes is quantitatively empty, and research-os-cloud-architecture.md#reliability-and-failure-behavior already ranks personal-state durability above the $0 invariant.

RadarCandidateItem.ttlExemptWhen: ttlExempt is true - set once when any note, save, or reference exists, and never cleared

identifierIndexReplica.description: Answers the sizing question research-item-identity.md#open-questions hands to T02. The identifier index is corpus-owned; a bounded, regenerable replica lives in DynamoDB because ingest resolution runs in the processor Lambda and cannot reach a local store.
identifierIndexReplica.replicaScope: entries for items inside the Radar TTL window, plus every ttlExempt item, and nothing else

transport.rationale: research-os-cloud-architecture.md#verified-allowances - SQS counts each 64 KB of payload as one request. Capping at exactly one chunk makes request consumption bounded by construction rather than by expectation.
transport.runtimeLeniency: A runtime consumer MUST ignore unknown properties inside payload rather than reject the message, so a producer may roll out ahead of a consumer. This schema declares payload bodies closed anyway, because the authoring-time and CI check is deliberately stricter than the runtime check: an accidental field must fail in CI, not silently ship.
transport.idempotency: At-least-once delivery. A consumer records idempotencyKey and applies each message at most once, enforced by a conditional write on attribute_not_exists - the same mechanism research-item-identity.md#the-decision uses for itemId minting.

versioningPolicy.contractVersion: Integer major on the ENVELOPE. Bumped only when the envelope shape changes. The envelope is closed (additionalProperties false) precisely so that this is the only way it can change.
versioningPolicy.payloadVersion: Integer major, PER MESSAGE TYPE, carried in the envelope so a consumer can route a body it cannot parse straight to the DLQ without parsing it.
versioningPolicy.additiveChange: Adding an optional property to a body: no version change.
versioningPolicy.breakingChange: Removing, renaming, retyping, or changing the meaning of a body property: payloadVersion major bump for that type only.
versioningPolicy.newMessageType: Adding a message type is additive; no contractVersion bump.
versioningPolicy.immutabilityWarning: This contract becomes immutable-in-practice the moment the first queue exists. Messages in flight cannot be re-versioned retroactively.

itemId.description: Canonical work identity. Opaque, minted once, never derived from mutable metadata. research-item-identity.md#canonical-item-identity.

messageId.description: ULID, same alphabet and prefix convention as itemId so a wrong-key bug is catchable by eye.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed. Never a local offset - the producer may run in any region.

dateString.description: Matches src/content.config.ts:10 so a date crossing into the projection needs no reformatting.

scheme.description: Cross-referenced against the scheme registry. Never an enum - shared-context.md section 4.

value.description: Normalized by normalizeExternalIdentifier before storage AND before index lookup.

provenance.description: Closed Zod enum by ADR, and the second deliberate exception to 'taxonomy is data, not code' alongside depth - shared-context.md section 4. A third value arriving through a data edit would silently change what TTL deletes, and TTL is destructive.

contractVersion.description: REQUIRED. Envelope major version. A consumer that does not recognise this value dead-letters the message without parsing the payload.

payloadVersion.description: Major version of THIS message type's body. Independent of contractVersion.

idempotencyKey.description: Deterministic for a given logical event. Redelivery of the same key is a no-op, enforced by a conditional write.

payload_candidateDiscovered_v1.description: Collector -> SQS -> processor. Carries enough to resolve identity and compute a content hash, and nothing else. No PDF, no full text - research-os-cloud-architecture.md#data-and-storage-strategy.

abstract.description: In transit and in the corpus only. NEVER written to DynamoDB. It is a content-hash input and a filtering input; it is not personal state and it is not a paper's full text.

payload_candidateProcessed_v1.description: Processor result. The only message that asserts an itemId.

resolution.description: 'merge-required' never merges. It raises a sameWorkAs claim for a human - research-item-identity.md#same-work-claims-and-their-confidence-vocabulary.

dedupKeys.description: Output of deriveDedupKey. Lookup keys for the identifier index - never an itemId.

observedContentHash.description: The hash the requester saw. A consumer that finds a different current hash re-reads rather than acting on stale input.

payload_personalStateMutation_v1.description: API -> DynamoDB. The only message that writes personal state. No principal identifier: single user.

oneOf.description: Clears savedAt. Never clears ttlExempt, and never deletes notes.

noteType.description: Note types are data, not an enum - research-discovery-system.md#research-notebook.

oneOf.description: Writes a new revision and sets revisionOf. The prior revision is retained - nothing is ever deleted.

personalStateItem.description: The hot DynamoDB item. Not a transport shape; declared here so the byte budget above is machine-checkable against a real attribute list.

ttlExempt.description: Set true once any note, save, or reference exists. Never cleared.

titleMirror.description: Capped at 160 BYTES after NFC normalization, not 160 characters. A 160-character Korean title is 480 UTF-8 bytes and alone breaks the 1 KB budget.
